body_markdown:
The news we’ve been waiting for—the return of the 6.2-liter supercharged Hellcat V-8 to the newest Dodge Charger—is almost, *almost* official. *Automotive News*[reports](https://www.autonews.com/manufacturing/an-stellantis-plots-v8-dodge-charger-launch-1012/) that it has “reviewed” a “planning document” written by Dodge to its suppliers that confirms the company’s plans to launch the Hellcat “at the end of 2027 for the 2028 model year.”


Dodge, for its part, ain’t saying you-know-what. As is standard practice in the auto industry, it refuses to comment on future product strategy. However, regular readers of this site will know that the signs are all there.


By way of background, the V-8 was nixed from Dodge and Ram’s North American portfolio by Stellantis CEO Carlos Tavares, a firm believer in cost-cutting and in our immediate all-electric future, who did not fully understand the U.S. market. When Tavares abruptly resigned in December of 2024, Tim Kuniskis unretired to lead Ram. The man famous for putting the 6.2-liter Hellcat in all the things started by reinstating more workaday Hemi variants, ordering that the 5.7-liter Hemi V-8 would return to Ram’s light-duty pickup by summer of 2025. Around that same time, he was promoted to lead Stellantis’ North American brands and the region’s marketing and retail strategy.


His influence is obvious. In short order, Ram[resurrected](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/jackpot-ram-trx-returns-for-2027-with-777-horsepower/) the Hellcat-powered, dune-pounding TRX performance truck, with even more hp (777, or an increase of 75) than its predecessor. Then, it rolled out a new version of an old idea: The[“Rumble Bee”](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/ram-goes-full-send-with-rumble-bee-sport-trucks/) line of V-8-powered street trucks, powered by the 5.7-liter, the 6.4-liter “Apache,” and the supercharged 6.2-liter V-8s, respectively. The last will go on sale in the first half of 2027, according to Ram.


Summary: Since Tavares’ departure, the Hemi is back in a big way … just not in the new, eighth-gen Charger. Yet.


Stellantis


The latest *AN* report is consistent with the hints Dodge has dropped in the last few years, though the detail about production volume (12,000/year) is new. As we noted[in January](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/a-new-hellcat-charger-is-possible-but-is-it-probable/) , Kuniskis has said that “the only way it makes sense to charge for \[an optional Hemi\] now is I have to go all the way up to a Hellcat,” noting that the 5.7-liter would be completely outgunned by the 550-hp inline-six. Since then, Dodge has rolled out[the six-cylinder, 600-hp Charger Super Bee](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/2027-dodge-charger-super-bee-pictures-specs-performance/) , thus filling in another rung in the performance hierarchy of its coupe/sedan. In other words, there’s plenty of room for another inline-six modified by SRT to maybe 650 or 700 hp *and* a crazy-powerful Hellcat model.


Dodge Charger Super Bee engine bay.


Stellantis


Back to practicalities: Would a supercharged 6.2-liter V-8 fit in an engine bay designed for an inline-six? Former *Hot Rod* editor and Roadkill co-host David Freiburger[let the cat out of the bag](https://www.hagerty.com/media/news/a-new-hellcat-charger-is-possible-but-is-it-probable/) as far back as November 2024. As Brandan Gillogly observed then, mass-producing such a vehicle is more complicated than engine-swapping a vehicle in your garage. Earlier this year, at the reveal of the Charger Six Pack, Dodge CEO Matt McAlear tiptoed awfully close to confirming that the 6.2 would fit, however. When asked, “theoretically,” whether a Hellcat would fit, he said: “Theoretically, I’ll let you come up here and take a look and get your tape measure out … but don’t be surprised if it would fit.”


We are so ready to be *not* surprised, Dodge! We’re ready right now!
